Angiofibromas ( Figure 1 ) are benign fibroblastic tumors that histologically comprise bland spindle cells in a variably myxoid to collagenous stroma with a prominent vascular network. They present as telangiectatic, skin colored to pink to red-brown, dome-shaped papules with a glistening surface that primarily occur in the central part of the face, especially the nose. They may be mistaken for acne but do not spontaneously resolve. in_text_mentions: Due to the diagnosis of MEN1, screening for pituitary tumor was performed at age 38. No physical signs of acromegaly were observed on examination. Sellar magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a central sellar nodule of 9 × 8 × 6 mm, initially considered to be a pituitary adenoma (Fig. 2).

Histopathological examination of the pituitary tissue revealed somatotroph hyperplasia (Fig. 3). findings.evidence: Caption: '(NMR) pituitary macroadenoma and left superior parietal extra-axial lesion compatible with meningioma.' In-text: 'A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) revealed a pituitary macroadenoma of 20 × 13 × 15 mm which spread to the right cavernous sinus, with displacement of the optic chiasm.'

panels.rationale: Single sagittal contrast brain MRI from the reported MEN1 case shows a sellar/suprasellar pituitary macroadenoma, with in-text support for cavernous sinus spread and optic chiasm displacement, plus an extra-axial parietal lesion compatible with meningioma. The disease-focused article title and caption support attribution of the pituitary macroadenoma to MEN1. The parietal meningioma is captioned but has no allowed vocabulary key, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. No age, ethnicity, skin surface, or annotations are assessable.

The caption describes enhancement in the ribs and the in-text states Fig. 2 shows 'metastases to the bones and liver' in a patient with MEN1 and multivisceral neuroendocrine tumor spread, supporting attribution to MEN1. B: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a heterogeneous enhancing lesion in the anterior mediastinum (white arrow). The caption groups it with the other hypervascular masses and the in-text describes 'multivisceral spread of the neuroendocrine tumors' in this MEN1 case; PET-CT also notes thymic hypermetabolism, supporting a thymic neuroendocrine lesion. C: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a hypervascular pancreatic mass (white arrow). Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor is a classic manifestation of MEN1, and the in-text confirms multivisceral neuroendocrine tumor spread in this MEN1 case.
